title: Amazon’s Bee launches two new personal AI devices, starting at $75
key_facts: Bee, acquired by Amazon last year, announced its first new products since the acquisition.
Bee Frontier: $74.99, wrist or clip, IP67 water resistance, up to seven days of battery, USB-C, dual microphones. Available now on Amazon.
Bee Eclipse: $99.99, credit-card-sized, magnetic attachment to a phone; available soon.
All devices give free summaries and 14 days of memory; Bee Pro costs $11.99 a month and adds Amazon.com and Alexa+ integrations and a personal chat assistant.
Audio is processed in real time and deleted; transcripts are encrypted with keys the device controls.
Optional link to Alexa Voice ID lets an Echo device trigger recording.
quote_evidence: The Bee Frontier is $74.99, compared with $159 for the Plaud Note (or $189 for the Note Pro), or $129 for the Pocket AI device.
Bee devices use a private computing security architecture, which doesn't store the raw audio from your conversations.
why_it_matters_hint: Cheaper always-listening AI note-takers, with privacy claims that rest on the company's own description.
